catalog_quote: Dunan has a three-way word-tone system for simple nouns. The tone domain is not the syllable nor the mora, but the word; one of the three distinctive melodies is mapped onto the word as a whole, regardless of its length. However, the actual tone-bearing unit is the syllable. The three word-tones High, Low and Falling, are also usually called A, B and C. The High tone is characterized by a high pitch on the last syllable of the words, with all preceding syllables high, except the first one in polysyllabic words. The Low tone is evenly low throughout the word. The Falling tone is similar to the High one, but the final syllable has a falling contour if it is heavy. If the last syllable of the word is light (i.e., is a (C)V syllable), it is pronounced with a high pitch, making it indistinguishable from a High-tone word, unless it is made heavy by attaching some extra phonological material, such as the inclusive clitic =n (‘even, too’). An unrealized final fall can also trigger a downstep of the following word (Uwano 2010). ... The difference of range between the high and low pitches is usually quite small in Dunan, which makes the assessment of each word’s tonal category a difficult task. Investigation of the tone system has barely begun, and tone will thus be left unmarked in most examples. [fn. 2] All the information on tone in this chapter thus comes from Uwano (2009, 2010, 2011).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word prosody is a lexical three-way word-tone (N-pattern accent) system: each simple noun belongs to class A/High (LH.H, final syllable high), B/Low (level low) or C/Falling (like A but with a fall on a heavy final syllable, neutralised with A on a light final syllable unless a clitic adds weight; an unrealised fall downsteps the next word). No stress is described; prominence location is not a positional stress rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress (no stress described at all).
new_statements.exceptions: Falling (C) tone is not realised on a light (C)V final syllable, making it indistinguishable from High unless e.g. inclusive =n is attached; super-heavy CVVN monosyllables are not resyllabified; some Low-tone verbs shift to Falling within their paradigm (metatony, three sub-patterns); pitch range between high and low is small; Uwano 2010 additionally notes items (mostly compounds) that fit none of the three patterns. Authors state tone is left unmarked in most examples and that all tone information comes from Uwano (2009, 2010, 2011).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the word (word-tone), TBU the syllable; Uwano 2010 frames the patterns over the bunsetsu (word + enclitics), e.g. C lowers a following particle/phrase. Data are citation forms and word+clitic forms from the Sonai dialect (Uwano's speaker b. 1919).
new_statements.identity_note: Yamada, Pellard & Shimoji 2015 describe Dunan (the endonym for Yonaguni, yona1241) as a whole; their tone data come from Uwano, whose materials (2010 ff.) are from the Sonai 祖納 settlement (speaker Ikema Nae, b. 1919). Nakazawa 2023 states dialect differences between the three settlements (Sonai, Higawa, Kubura) are negligible apart from Okinawan influence in Kubura. No sub-glottocodes involved.

new_statements.relation_note: Same object as the catalog's existing statement (Yamada, Pellard & Shimoji 2015: three-way word-tone system, melody mapped onto the whole word). Uwano calls it a '3型アクセント' (three-pattern accent, types A/B/C on the accent unit) rather than 'word tone', but describes the same three word-level pitch melodies and never posits stress; so the type is compatible (terminological difference only). It adds: pitch realisation of the three types, the accent-unit domain including multi-unit compounds, absence of a compound accent law, and the length/weight-based predictability of loanword class (<=3 morae C; >=4 morae B unless heavy final syllable -> C).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Yonaguni (Sonai) has a three-pattern word accent system: every accent unit (a simple word, or each unit of a multi-unit compound) carries one of three pitch patterns A (=; no fall, like Tokyo unaccented), B (_; low, with a rise on a following element) or C (]; fall / half-fall at the unit end). The pattern is a property of the whole unit, not of a particular syllable, and nothing is said about stress or dynamic prominence. Loanwords: up to 3 morae take C; 4 or more morae take B unless the final syllable is heavy (ends in N or a long vowel), in which case C. Native compounds show no 'compound accent law' (the first element's class does not predict the compound's class) and productive place-name compounds usually form two or three accent units, each keeping its own pattern.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None reported; multi-unit compounds carry one pattern per accent unit (up to three units, e.g. zjosji]taNki]daigaku_ 'women's junior college' with two falls, 2015: 168).
new_statements.exceptions: Loanword exceptions listed: zuboN_, donau_, buriKi_, razji'o_ are B although 3 morae or fewer (2014: 76); 'aribai_, dezaiN_ are B despite a heavy final syllable; korokKe] is C despite a light final (2014: 76); in Ikema Ryuichi's data 8-10 short words are B (demа, ka:do, koNbi, suki:, zuboN, cji:mu, terebi, bakecu) and karori:, patoka:, fassjoN, merodi: are B despite heavy finals; A type is rare in loanwords (only 5 sure cases, 2016: 72-73). Simple word and compound with the same first element often differ in class ('no shiki-hozon'), and A-type first elements of '-ken' are often realised as C (2015: 167).
new_statements.identity_note: All three Uwano papers describe the Sonai (祖納) variety of Yonaguni, from two speakers: Ikema Nae (b. 1919, Sonai) and, for the 2015 compound data and the 2016 loanword data, her son Ikema Ryuichi (b. 1950, Sonai). The 2016 paper reports that the two speakers agree on 13 of 14 shared loanword items. tone_statements.quote: 与那国方言は母音音素が /a/, /i/, /u/ の 3 つ，子音音素が /p/, /b/, /m/, /t/, /t/, /d/, /n/, /r/, /c/ [ʦˀ], /s/, /k/, /k/, /g/, /ŋ/, /h/, /ʼ/ の 16 個で他に半母音音素 /j/, /w/ と撥音 /N/ を有する … A 型，B 型，C 型の三型アクセント体系であり，A 型は概ね高平調，B 型は概ね低平調で，C 型は A 型に似るが後続するアクセント単位のピッチを下げる（上野 2010）。
tone_statements.translation: The Yonaguni dialect has three vowel phonemes /a/, /i/, /u/, 16 consonant phonemes /p, b, m, t, t, d, n, r, c [tsˀ], s, k, k, g, ŋ, h, ʼ/, plus the semivowel phonemes /j/, /w/ and the moraic nasal /N/ … It is a three-pattern accent system of type A, type B and type C: type A is roughly a high level tone, type B roughly a low level tone, and type C resembles type A but lowers the pitch of the following accent unit (Uwano 2010).
tone_statements.locator: p. 90, sec. 2.2 与那国方言; accent classes of verb forms also pp. 103-104 sec. 5.1 + fn. 44
tone_statements.summary: Three-pattern word accent (types A, B, C): A roughly high level, B roughly low level, C like A but lowering the pitch of the next accent unit (after Uwano 2010); verb forms differ by accent class.

tone_statements.quote: 与那国方言が三型アクセント体系であることは平山・中本 (1964) で明らかにされている。本発表では上野 (2010a) などの一連の先行研究に従い，A 型，B 型，C 型のラベルを与える。A 型は概ね高平調，B 型は概ね低平調で，C 型は A 型に似るが後続するアクセント単位を下げる。 … 単純語を調査した結果，両話者とも先行研究と同様の A 型，B 型，C 型の三型アクセントを保持しており，A 型は下がり目がなく，B 型は低平調，C 型は文節末に下がり目がある。 … A 型を無核型，B 型と C 型を有核型と考える。
tone_statements.translation: That the Yonaguni dialect has a three-pattern accent system was established by Hirayama & Nakamoto (1964). Following Uwano (2010a) and related prior studies, this paper labels the patterns Type A, Type B and Type C. Type A is roughly a high level pitch, Type B roughly a low level pitch, and Type C resembles Type A but lowers the following accent unit. ... The survey of simplex words shows that both speakers retain the same three-pattern accent A, B, C as in prior studies: Type A has no pitch fall, Type B is low level, Type C has a fall at the end of the phrase. ... We regard Type A as unaccented (kernel-less) and Types B and C as accented (having a kernel).
tone_statements.locator: p. 133 sec. 3.1 与那国方言のアクセント体系; p. 134 sec. 4.2 調査結果; p. 137 sec. 5.3 B型と有核型
tone_statements.summary: Three-pattern word accent: A high level, B low level, C high with a phrase-final fall that lowers the next unit; confirmed on two speakers with pitch tracks; A analysed unaccented, B and C accented.

tone_statements.quote: Dunan has a lexical tone system where melodies apply to whole word forms, including any following clitic. Dunan has a three-way opposition between a High (H), Low (L), and Falling (F) word tone.8 8 Phonetically, High tone words have a high pitch throughout except for the first syllable of polysyllabic words. Falling tone words are similar to High tone ones, except that they have a falling pitch on the last syllable if it is heavy and they can trigger downstep on a following word. Low tone words have a low pitch throughout.
tone_statements.locator: p. 39, sec. 5.1 'Overview of the tone system' with footnote 8 (metatony sec. 5.2-5.3, pp. 40-41; tone marking convention fn. 3, p. 32)
tone_statements.summary: Lexical word-tone system: three melodies, High, Low and Falling, over the word plus clitics; Falling words can downstep the next word; some verbs alternate L and F within the paradigm (metatony).

tone_statements.quote: Ａ，Ｂ，Ｃの３つのアクセント型については，それぞれＡ型：=， Ｂ型：_，C型： ]をアクセント単位の末尾に付して示す。一部，前回までの調査と今回とで食い違いが見られた項目があるが，それらについては，未調査語彙とともに，今後の調査に俟つ。また，複合語のアクセントは，１単位形か２単位形か，後者の場合にその後部要素の型をどう認定するか等，なお検討を要するが，それについてもいずれ詳しく取り扱う機会を得たい。
tone_statements.translation: As for the three accent types A, B and C, they are shown by attaching, respectively, type A: =, type B: _, type C: ] to the end of the accent unit. For some items discrepancies were found between the previous surveys and this one; those, together with the vocabulary not yet surveyed, await future investigation. Also, the accent of compounds -- whether a one-unit or a two-unit form, and in the latter case how to identify the type of the second element, etc. -- still needs examination, and I hope to treat that in detail on another occasion.

tone_statements.summary: Three lexical accent types (A, B, C) assigned to accent units (words); c. 1,300 Sonai nominal forms from one speaker b. 1919 marked for type; pitch shapes of the types not described here.

tone_statements.quote: Ａ，Ｂ，Ｃの３つの型からなる３型アクセントである与那国方言（上野2010）について，その動詞活用形のアクセントをこれまで２回にわたって発表して来た。 … そのアクセントの交替パターンが大きく６種類に分けられることを明らかにした。終止形がＡ型であれば他の活用形もすべてＡ型になる。 … 今回は，活用形の数は下記の７つに限定し，単語を300語強に増やした資料を提示する。最後にそれぞれのパターンを，上野（2011b）に従ってA, Bb, Bc, Bcc, Bccc, Cで示す。 … アクセントは，下記の記号をそれぞれのアクセント単位の末尾に示した。 =（Ａ型），_（Ｂ型），]（Ｃ型）
tone_statements.translation: Concerning the Yonaguni dialect, which is a three-pattern accent system consisting of the three patterns A, B and C (Uwano 2010), I have so far published the accent of its conjugated verb forms twice. ... [I] showed that the accent alternation patterns divide broadly into six types. If the conclusive form is pattern A, all other conjugated forms are also pattern A. ... This time the conjugated forms are limited to the seven below and the material is enlarged to a little over 300 words. At the end each pattern is shown as A, Bb, Bc, Bcc, Bccc, C following Uwano (2011b). ... Accent is shown with the following marks at the end of each accent unit: = (pattern A), _ (pattern B), ] (pattern C).
tone_statements.locator: pp. 57-58, untitled introduction (system statement p. 57, accent notation p. 58)
tone_statements.summary: Three-pattern (A, B, C) word accent: each accent unit takes one of three lexical patterns, marked on 300+ verbs in 7 conjugated forms; pitch shapes of A/B/C not described here (refers to Uwano 2010).

tone_statements.quote: 沖縄県与那国町祖納（そない）のアクセントについては、拙論（2010b）において、音節を単位とし（私の用語で言えば、音節が拍を形成し）、文節末音節の軽重が対立の顕現に関与する興味深い体系であり … アクセントは、Ａ型を =、Ｂ型を ]、Ｃ型を _ で示した。活用形のアクセントで最も目に付く特徴は、３型アクセントでありながら、終止形（本稿の「現在止」）がＡ型のものは各活用形もＡ型を取るものの、終止形がＢ型とＣ型はそれぞれの系列で一貫するのではなく、互いにＣ型とＢ型が混じる点である。 … この特徴は、やはり３型アクセントの隠岐島諸方言と共通する。
tone_statements.translation: As for the accent of Sonai, Yonaguni Town, Okinawa Prefecture, in my paper (2010b) [I stated that] it is an interesting system that takes the syllable as its unit (in my terms, the syllable forms the beat) and in which the weight of the phrase-final syllable is involved in the manifestation of the contrast ... Accent is shown with = for pattern A, ] for pattern B and _ for pattern C. The most striking feature of the accent of conjugated forms is that, although this is a three-pattern accent system, verbs whose conclusive form ('present conclusive' here) is pattern A take pattern A in every conjugated form, whereas those whose conclusive form is B or C are not consistent within their series but mix C and B with each other. ... This feature is shared with the Oki Islands dialects, likewise three-pattern accent systems.
tone_statements.locator: p. 105 and p. 107, はじめに (introduction)
tone_statements.summary: Sonai Yonaguni: a three-pattern accent system (patterns A, B, C) with the syllable as unit; phrase-final syllable weight affects how the contrast surfaces; verb paradigms mix B and C.

tone_statements.quote: 西銘氏のデータから想定する動詞継絡相の音韻論的なアクセント規則は次の通りである。〇は短音節、Cつは長音節(①音節で②モーラの長さ)を表し、終止形を-buNで統一する。③型アクセントと仮定する。 … (高平型 … (低平型 … (上昇型) … 高平型は高く始まって進むことに音韻論的な弁別があるとし、最初から②音節目等に現われる下がりには音韻論的な弁別機能を考えない。低平型は低く始まって進むことに音韻的な弁別があるとする。上昇型は、-buNの前が短音節二つの場合、①音餐目から②音節目にかけて上昇することに音韻的な弁別があるものとし … 崎原氏のデータから想定する動詞継続相の音韻論的なよアクセント規則は次の通りである。②型アクセントと仮定する。
tone_statements.translation: The phonological accent rules for the verb continuative aspect posited from Mr Nishime's data are as follows. O = short syllable, the oval = long syllable (one syllable, two morae long); citation form unified as -buN. A 3-pattern accent is assumed. [schemas: (high-level type) (low-level type) (rising type)] The high-level type is phonologically distinguished by starting high and continuing so; falls appearing from the 2nd syllable on have no distinctive function. sources.quote: Dunan has a three-way word-tone system for simple nouns. The tone domain is not the syllable nor the mora, but the word; one of the three distinctive melodies is mapped onto the word as a whole, regardless of its length. However, the actual tone-bearing unit is the syllable. The three word-tones High, Low and Falling, are also usually called A, B and C. The High tone is characterized by a high pitch on the last syllable of the words, with all preceding syllables high, except the first one in polysyllabic words. The Low tone is evenly low throughout the word. The Falling tone is similar to the High one, but the final syllable has a falling contour if it is heavy.

tone.translation: As for the accent of Sonai, Yonaguni Town, Okinawa Prefecture, in my paper (2010b) [I stated that] it is an interesting system that takes the syllable as its unit (in my terms, the syllable forms the beat) and in which the weight of the phrase-final syllable is involved in the manifestation of the contrast ... Accent is shown with = for pattern A, ] for pattern B and _ for pattern C. The most striking feature of the accent of conjugated forms is that, although this is a three-pattern accent system, verbs whose conclusive form ('present conclusive' here) is pattern A take pattern A in every conjugated form, whereas those whose conclusive form is B or C are not consistent within their series but mix C and B with each other. ... This feature is shared with the Oki Islands dialects, likewise three-pattern accent systems.

tone.translation: The phonological accent rules for the verb continuative aspect posited from Mr Nishime's data are as follows. O = short syllable, the oval = long syllable (one syllable, two morae long); citation form unified as -buN. A 3-pattern accent is assumed. [schemas: (high-level type) (low-level type) (rising type)] The high-level type is phonologically distinguished by starting high and continuing so; falls appearing from the 2nd syllable on have no distinctive function.
